content:
There are two tactics doing the same: repeat' refine And.intro ?_ ?_.

  • and_intros defined in Core
  • split_ands defined in Batteries

Shouldn't we keep just one of them, and have the other deprecated? Which name do you think is better? Which one of them should I tell my students about?
I didn't know about either

Honestly, just looking at the title, I thought one was for And.intro and the other was for cases . I think at least in this sense and_intros is less ambiguous (and it is in core, so we'll have an easier time deprecating split_ands)

I like split_ands, it matches split_ifs
FWIW it's also what Alex Kontorovich taught to his real-analysis students; #mathlib4 > `obtain` syntax @ 💬

Robin Arnez said:

Honestly, just looking at the title, I thought one was for And.intro and the other was for cases . I think at least in this sense and_intros is less ambiguous (and it is in core, so we'll have an easier time deprecating split_ands)

True, reminds me of the two bugfixes I have seen you here submitting into core (probably, there are more of those I have not noticed), and they are not merged yet :sweat_smile:

On the other hand, so far there is one "vote" for each option so far, so let me create a poll.

/poll How a tactic splitting the goal a ∧ b ∧ c ∧ d should be called?
and_intros
split_ands
other (I post below)
Oops, haven't realized that polls allow adding options automatically, ignore the "other" option.

since they haven't been mentioned, note that there are also some other ways to get the same effect:

import Mathlib.Tactic
example : True ∧ True ∧ True ∧ True := by
  refine ⟨?_,?_,?_,?_⟩ -- also works without mathlib
  all_goals trivial

example : True ∧ True ∧ True ∧ True := by
  constructorm* (_ ∧ _)
  all_goals trivial
Fair to mention, but I would like to settle the question of And specifically. refine can be used instead of almost anything...
But feel free to add an option to the poll that no And-specific tactic should exist (which would be a jump from 2 to 0 :grinning: )
i suppose i'm arguing that ideally we don't have a tactic only for splitting and... Anyway, i voted on my preference between the options, and added the option of removing both.

I'm rather fond of split_ands. I use it any time I'm dealing with more than a single conjunction. Lots of other ways of achieving the same end, but it's hard to beat split_ands for clarity . Does exactly what it says on the tin!
there are many of these duplications between Core and Mathlib with superficial differences. use and exists comes to mind off the top of my head.
use and exists have different behaviors however

Indeed, I was asking about use / exists before. There the conclusion was that everyone uses use, and exists is mostly forgotten, although Mathlib also adds the tactic existsi, which is more predictable (is not trying to run discharger). Here the situation is even more paradoxical as it seems that Core and Batteries define the exact same tactic with a different name, and both of them are a bit forgotten :slight_smile:

Possible upgrade paths:

  • if we want only split_ands, I am happy to move it upstream to lean4, and deprecate and_intros in favour of it (or approve a PR doing so)
  • if we want to remove both, if someone could formulate a deprecation warning message suggesting what a putative user should do instead, I am happy to install that in and_intros (or approve a PR doing so), and later remove.

Despite the poll says we don't need it, I second David's view that there is a value in having such beginner tactic. Both refine and constructorm* require deeper understanding. So I would rather go with replacing and_intros with split_ands. Opposing views? (from people voting "we don't need it")
refine is amazing and should be taught to beginners on day 1

IMO split_ands should be a teaching tactic that people add to their own lean4game repos.
But: Rocq has split as an alternative for constructor when the goal has exactly one constructor. "Generalizing" split_ands to a new split would be nice, and would solve #lean4 > `constructor` papercut. But we'd have to find a different word since split already exists and does something else
Do you think it is a good idea to define your own tactic just for the sake of teaching (say in Natural Number Game), and when the students try it out in Lean 4 Web, they get an undefined tactic?
refine is nice, but forcing beginners to deal with pattern syntax in the beginning is not a nice learning experience.

Snir Broshi said:

refine is amazing and should be taught to beginners on day 1

Just for the record, I did teach refine as soon as I introduced tactics -- just after inductive types & curry-howard correspondence. Not everyone chooses such teaching path though.
I would ideally want a tactic that splits all constructors, not just those of a certain type. Finding the exact refine incantation for a long, nested statement can sometimes be a quite tedious task.

Mirek Olšák said:

Do you think it is a good idea to define your own tactic just for the sake of teaching (say in Natural Number Game), and when the students try it out in Lean 4 Web, they get an undefined tactic?

Yes, many games already modify existing tactics (to weaken them) which means proofs that work in the game work differently in Lean 4 Web. I don't think adding a new tactic is that much of a stretch from this, even though it means that you'll get "unknown tactic" rather than possibly helpful errors and a docstring.

Shreyas Srinivas said:

refine is nice, but forcing beginners to deal with pattern syntax in the beginning is not a nice learning experience.

As a once-beginner, I couldn't develop concret idea of what apply does until I saw the pattern syntax of refine. Now whenever I see apply I just mentally append it with a bunch of ?_
Ditto Weiyi. I would also really enjoy a syntax like rconstructor And that would also work as e.g. rconstructor Iff or rconstructor And Iff to recurse on different structures.

Alex Meiburg said:

Ditto Weiyi. I would also really enjoy a syntax like rconstructor And that would also work as e.g. rconstructor Iff or rconstructor And Iff to recurse on different structures.

You can do constructorm* And that also works for e.g. constructorm* Iff and constructorm* And, Iff.

I think one needs constructorm* Add _ _ or constructorm* Iff _ _actually.

When proving goals such as P ↔ Q it would be nice to have a tactic that does the maximal expansion of constructor and intro, which in this case would be refine ⟨ fun h ↦ ?_, fun h ↦ ?_ ⟩. In the spirit of split_ands, this could be split_all with h, perhaps.
